To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the definition of genetic literacy is the ability to use the knowledge of genetics to understand the implications of genetics for one's personal life, the lives of others, and the society as a whole.
the definition of genetic literacy should include the knowledge that is needed to understand the relevance and implications of genetic applications for society and for the individual.
Genetic literacy is knowledge of genetic concepts and their applications in medicine, forensics, and agriculture, and of their societal, cultural, and ethical implications."
In summary, our research is concerned with
a consensus reaching approach to determine the definition of genetic literacy that is required from a twenty first century citizen.
the development of a conceptual framework for the genetic literacy that is required from a 21st century citizen.
the question of what knowledge is needed from a twenty-first century citizen to make informed decisions on genetic issues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a twenty first century citizen needs a genetic literacy that consists of nine conceptual components, three sociological components, and four components related to epistemology and philosophy of science.

a genetic literate person should be able to understand the genetic aspects of seven cases: (1) genetic disease, (2) genetic testing and screening, (3) genetic modification of crops and food, (4) genetically modified organisms in nature, (5) gene editing, (6) forensic applications, and (7) genetic privacy and discrimination.

a twenty-first century citizen needs to be able to understand the concepts of inheritance, variation and mutation; the structure and function of genes and DNA; and the basic mechanisms of genetic processes such as gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

genetic literacy for the twenty first century citizen should be a combination of knowledge and skills, which are necessary for decision making on issues that involve genetics and which is acquired by a combination of learning in and out of school.

the knowledge components of genetics are relevant for a twenty first century citizen because they help to understand the complexity of the genetic information in the context of the society in which they live.
the participants agreed on the importance of genetic literacy and the need to teach it in the school curriculum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the framework can serve as a basis for a consensus definition of genetic literacy that is required from a twenty first century citizen.

the knowledge of genetics required from a twenty-first century citizen is more than a basic understanding of the concepts involved, it also requires a critical approach and a reflection of the social and ethical implications of the use of genetics in society.
genetic literacy should not be limited to a specific field of genetics.
